channel.title: gtree Blog — Parallel Claude Code, git worktrees and AI teamwork
channel.description: How to run several Claude Code sessions at once, isolate them with git worktrees, and keep two AI agents from editing the same file — guides and gtree features.

item.title: Why gtree Isn't Electron: 24 MB, Window in 0.2 Seconds
item.description: A native Rust + GPUI app with no bundled browser or Node: 24 MB download, window in about 0.2 s, ~100 MB idle memory. Measured numbers and how we got them.

item.title: How to Undo Claude Code Changes, Even After the Session Ends
item.description: Undo AI coding changes three ways: git, Claude Code's /rewind, and gtree's per-turn checkpoints, which restore any turn's files even after the session is closed.

item.title: Two AI Agents, One File: Stop Them Overwriting Each Other
item.description: Two AI agents editing the same file? Spot overlaps with plain git, or let the agents message each other and agree who goes first. Works with Claude Code and Codex.

item.title: How to Know When Claude Code Is Waiting for Your Approval
item.description: Claude Code stops whenever it needs permission. Get notified with a Notification hook, and see which of your sessions is waiting on one screen.

item.title: How to Run Multiple Claude Code Sessions with Git Worktree
item.description: Give each Claude Code session its own git worktree so parallel AIs never share a folder. The exact commands, the gotchas, and how to skip the busywork.
